title: Phase 2：OEIS A294646 猜想「a(n) 不會是 2n−2」的反例 n = 9814447404，另兩半為古典結果

A294646-not-2n-2.proof: n = 9814447404: 2n+1 = 19628894809 = 367*53484727 divides 3*2^(2n)+1, so a(n) = 2n-2 (Lean kernel check a294646_counterexample, core only; Python big-int check). Least counterexample: structural search (scan.c, all admissible primes p < 2e6, cofactors <= 1e9) is complete for 2n+1 <= 6.1e10 and finds only this one; brute force over all odd m < 1e10 agrees.

A294646-not-2.proof: Classical: m > 1 never divides 2^m - 1 (least prime factor vs order of 2). Paper proof only; brute force m < 1e10.

A294646-not-2n.proof: Classical: m > 1 never divides 2^(m-1) + 1 (2-adic valuation of the order of 2). Paper proof only; brute force m < 1e10.

novelty.note: No report of this counterexample in the OEIS entry, an OEIS term search, or web search. The method (necessary congruences + search) is standard; the result is a single explicit counterexample. Not claimed as a new theorem; MathSciNet/zbMATH not searched.
